text:
Anya: quick sync — looping folks on a slimline operator proposal for dedicated pool leases. want to avoid the heavy reservation model while keeping predictable perf for tiered customers.
Micah: curious — what's 'slimline' here? shorter commitments or lighter semantics?
Anya: both. idea: short TTL leases (30s-5m) + a lightweight contract object that captures 'min-rate' and 'grace-window' instead of full reserved capacity. 
James: so more like soft-commitments that give the scheduler a hint? vs hard capacity holds? :thinking_face:
Anya: exactly. scheduler treats a contract as preference with time decay. if contract expires we fallback without a painful eviction cascade.
Lia: how do we prevent noisy tenants from gaming this by continuously renewing leases?
Micah: we can add a backoff penalty on renewal frequency and escalate cost/priority when they renew aggressively.
Anya: proposal sketch: 
```
contract {
  tenant_id: string
  min_qps: int  # hint for steady-state throughput
  max_burst: int
  ttl_seconds: int
  renewal_count: int
}
```
renewal_count increments per renewal; after thresholds we drop soft-priority.
James: ok. what about headroom prewarming? slimline contracts should still allow brief warmups without claiming whole GPU.
Anya: we add transient "warmth tokens" that are ephemeral and not persisted across operator restarts. tokens are cheap and can be revoked.
Micah: operator split question: which component owns contract reconciliation? current operator handles full admission + eviction. can we split responsibility so a "contract manager" owns TTL bookkeeping and the core operator owns placement?
Lia: split seems cleaner — contract manager can publish intent signals to a small API consumed by placement controller. reduces blast radius.
James: downside is added eventual consistency. how strict are we about SLOs during transient mismatch?
Anya: plan is best-effort for burst; for guaranteed lanes we still provide reserved capacity under existing dedicated pools (no change). slimline is opt-in for non-guaranteed tiers.
Micah: metrics we should emit: contract_count_by_tenant, renewals_per_min, avg_ttl, revoke_rate, placement_mismatch_rate.
Lia: ops playbook — on high revoke_rate we should auto-throttle renewals and send an alert to SEs. include a diff for tenant above 95th percentile renewals.
James: one more: how do CLI/API semantics look? request body should be tiny. example: `POST /contracts {tenant: "acme", min_qps: 10, ttl: 120}` returns contract_id + expires_at. renewal uses same endpoint.
Anya: exact. also include server-side sanity checks: min_qps <= tenant_quota and ttl bounded [30, 300].
Micah: we need a cheap leader election for contract manager in HA. can reuse operator-leader lock.
Lia: rollouts: start internal-only with 2 tenants and progressive enablement. measure cost delta and mismatch rate.
James: question on billing — renewals could be abused. recommend adding a small metered charge for renewal beyond N freebies/month. aligns incentives.
Anya: agreed. add to product/finance follow-up.
orch-bot: deploy-check: contract-manager:v0.1 image built, no infra changes required./logs -> https://ci/redwood/1234 :white_check_mark:
Micah: thanks — i'll prototype the contract manager sketch and share an RFC.
Lia: i'll draft rollout playbook and alerts.
James: i'll scope the billing hook and add to pricing doc.
Anya: great. next steps: prototype, small canary, telemetry. tagging @micah @lia @james for visibility. :rocket:
